analysis.assessment: Incident evaluation-case concerns newly available LIMS result LAB-0225 for batch BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, in process since 2024-12-01T06:40Z, no disposition recorded): test relative_bioburden_signal, unit action-limit ratio, numerical_result 1.23 vs action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7 (123.00% of the action limit, +0.23 units), status 'action', sample collected 2024-12-01T10:40:00Z, result available exactly at the 12:00:00Z cutoff. LAB-0225 is the only new action-level result and the highest value in the scoped package. Near-simultaneous records bracket it: PRE-LAB-001 (same batch, sample 10:45Z, 0.79, alert, 79.00% of the action limit), environmental monitoring EM-0075 (10:50Z, 0.71, alert, process support area, 101.43% of its alert limit), and four historian margin parameters (08:40Z-11:10Z) all within expected ranges (differential_pressure_margin 0.9615 carries severity 'low' against its 1.0 expected high limit). The 0.44-unit (55.70%) difference between two samples drawn five minutes apart is unexplained by any metadata in scope. No independent confirmation or completed human review of LAB-0225 exists in the scoped records: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates the LIMS values, lims_review_local.csv mirrors the status ('action', 123.0 % of limit) with no reviewer/date/comment, and the review PDFs do not mention LAB-0225 (one is a self-described duplicate export with degraded OCR pending human visual review). No open deviations, no open work orders (all six VESSEL-01 orders closed, latest 2024-10-25), no out-of-range historian values, and only a routine operator batch check (07:55Z) are recorded. Competing explanations remain open and none is confirmed: true transient excursion (H-1), analytical/sample-handling artifact (H-2, with a documented historical invalidation precedent LAB-0043 at 1.06), recording error (H-3, weak), facility-level pattern (H-4, contradicted by dispersed old records and closed maintenance), or sampling/method difference between the paired draws (H-5). Human-reviewed next steps: SOP result review of LAB-0225 with a retest/invalidation decision, BATCH-075 disposition impact assessment, assay QC retrieval, and follow-up of the process-support-area alert. Proposed severity MEDIUM (advisory; the configured routing policy determines final severity). This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or manufacturing change.

draft_report.assessment: Incident evaluation-case concerns newly available LIMS result LAB-0225 for batch BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, in process since 2024-12-01T06:40Z, no disposition recorded): test relative_bioburden_signal, unit action-limit ratio, numerical_result 1.23 vs action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7 (123.00% of the action limit, +0.23 units), status 'action', sample collected 2024-12-01T10:40:00Z, result available exactly at the 12:00:00Z cutoff. LAB-0225 is the only new action-level result and the highest value in the scoped package. Near-simultaneous records bracket it: PRE-LAB-001 (same batch, sample 10:45Z, 0.79, alert, 79.00% of the action limit), environmental monitoring EM-0075 (10:50Z, 0.71, alert, process support area, 101.43% of its alert limit), and four historian margin parameters (08:40Z-11:10Z) all within expected ranges (differential_pressure_margin 0.9615 carries severity 'low' against its 1.0 expected high limit). The 0.44-unit (55.70%) difference between two samples drawn five minutes apart is unexplained by any metadata in scope. No independent confirmation or completed human review of LAB-0225 exists in the scoped records: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates the LIMS values, lims_review_local.csv mirrors the status ('action', 123.0 % of limit) with no reviewer/date/comment, and the review PDFs do not mention LAB-0225 (one is a self-described duplicate export with degraded OCR pending human visual review). No open deviations, no open work orders (all six VESSEL-01 orders closed, latest 2024-10-25), no out-of-range historian values, and only a routine operator batch check (07:55Z) are recorded. Competing explanations remain open and none is confirmed: true transient excursion (H-1), analytical/sample-handling artifact (H-2, with a documented historical invalidation precedent LAB-0043 at 1.06), recording error (H-3, weak), facility-level pattern (H-4, contradicted by dispersed old records and closed maintenance), or sampling/method difference between the paired draws (H-5). Human-reviewed next steps: SOP result review of LAB-0225 with a retest/invalidation decision, BATCH-075 disposition impact assessment, assay QC retrieval, and follow-up of the process-support-area alert. Proposed severity MEDIUM (advisory; the configured routing policy determines final severity). This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or manufacturing change.

draft_report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: four independent record systems carry BATCH-075 records on 2024-12-01 between 06:40Z and 11:10Z, and the lab-side systems express one normalized relative bioburden signal in three forms - absolute action-limit ratio (LIMS 1.23/0.79), a duplicated re-export (microbiology_results.xlsx), and percent-of-limit (lims_review_local 123.0%). The action-level peak (10:40Z sample) is bracketed by alert-level results (0.79 at 10:45Z, 0.71 environmental at 10:50Z) while historian margins stay within expected ranges; the only non-normal historian severity for this batch is 'low' on differential_pressure_margin (0.9615 vs high limit 1.0) at 09:10Z, a temporal association that establishes no causal direction. Systematic recording caveats: the package exports carry no elapsed process clocks (1049 of 1051 screened series flagged missing_source_time; the deterministic align_series check rejects LIMS-vs-historian alignment for lack of visible source time coordinates), so chronology rests on explicit zoned record timestamps. Two worksheets are re-exports of canonical LIMS data and provide no independent assurance; the scanned review document is an image-only PDF whose degraded OCR self-identifies as a duplicate export and remains pending human visual review. Cohort exceptions: LAB-0225 (1.23) exceeds every historical result; past action-level results either stood (LAB-0010, SYN-0004, 1.08) or were invalidated after review (LAB-0043, SYN-0014, 1.06), so both outcomes are precedented. Six further SYN entities carry historical alert-level results (all status alert, below the action limit), and each was followed by a substantially lower repeat result within about a day; for three of them the same-day environmental record is also elevated. All 15 related units were read at row level as cohort context. Missing evidence, not any confirmed cause, is the main limit: no assay QC, method/analyst metadata, reviewer identity/date, sampling SOP for the paired draws, retest results, or post-cutoff records are available in scope. All 311 screening units carry an explicit review disposition (34 investigated, 277 reviewed with no material signal).

analysis.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: four independent record systems carry BATCH-075 records on 2024-12-01 between 06:40Z and 11:10Z, and the lab-side systems express one normalized relative bioburden signal in three forms - absolute action-limit ratio (LIMS 1.23/0.79), a duplicated re-export (microbiology_results.xlsx), and percent-of-limit (lims_review_local 123.0%). The action-level peak (10:40Z sample) is bracketed by alert-level results (0.79 at 10:45Z, 0.71 environmental at 10:50Z) while historian margins stay within expected ranges; the only non-normal historian severity for this batch is 'low' on differential_pressure_margin (0.9615 vs high limit 1.0) at 09:10Z, a temporal association that establishes no causal direction. Systematic recording caveats: the package exports carry no elapsed process clocks (1049 of 1051 screened series flagged missing_source_time; the deterministic align_series check rejects LIMS-vs-historian alignment for lack of visible source time coordinates), so chronology rests on explicit zoned record timestamps. Two worksheets are re-exports of canonical LIMS data and provide no independent assurance; the scanned review document is an image-only PDF whose degraded OCR self-identifies as a duplicate export and remains pending human visual review. Cohort exceptions: LAB-0225 (1.23) exceeds every historical result; past action-level results either stood (LAB-0010, SYN-0004, 1.08) or were invalidated after review (LAB-0043, SYN-0014, 1.06), so both outcomes are precedented. Six further SYN entities carry historical alert-level results (all status alert, below the action limit), and each was followed by a substantially lower repeat result within about a day; for three of them the same-day environmental record is also elevated. All 15 related units were read at row level as cohort context. Missing evidence, not any confirmed cause, is the main limit: no assay QC, method/analyst metadata, reviewer identity/date, sampling SOP for the paired draws, retest results, or post-cutoff records are available in scope. All 311 screening units carry an explicit review disposition (34 investigated, 277 reviewed with no material signal).

workflow.assessment: Incident evaluation-case concerns newly available LIMS result LAB-0225 for batch BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, in process since 2024-12-01T06:40Z, no disposition recorded): test relative_bioburden_signal, unit action-limit ratio, numerical_result 1.23 vs action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7 (123.00% of the action limit, +0.23 units), status 'action', sample collected 2024-12-01T10:40:00Z, result available exactly at the 12:00:00Z cutoff. LAB-0225 is the only new action-level result and the highest value in the scoped package. Near-simultaneous records bracket it: PRE-LAB-001 (same batch, sample 10:45Z, 0.79, alert, 79.00% of the action limit), environmental monitoring EM-0075 (10:50Z, 0.71, alert, process support area, 101.43% of its alert limit), and four historian margin parameters (08:40Z-11:10Z) all within expected ranges (differential_pressure_margin 0.9615 carries severity 'low' against its 1.0 expected high limit). The 0.44-unit (55.70%) difference between two samples drawn five minutes apart is unexplained by any metadata in scope. No independent confirmation or completed human review of LAB-0225 exists in the scoped records: microbiology_results.xlsx duplicates the LIMS values, lims_review_local.csv mirrors the status ('action', 123.0 % of limit) with no reviewer/date/comment, and the review PDFs do not mention LAB-0225 (one is a self-described duplicate export with degraded OCR pending human visual review). No open deviations, no open work orders (all six VESSEL-01 orders closed, latest 2024-10-25), no out-of-range historian values, and only a routine operator batch check (07:55Z) are recorded. Competing explanations remain open and none is confirmed: true transient excursion (H-1), analytical/sample-handling artifact (H-2, with a documented historical invalidation precedent LAB-0043 at 1.06), recording error (H-3, weak), facility-level pattern (H-4, contradicted by dispersed old records and closed maintenance), or sampling/method difference between the paired draws (H-5). Human-reviewed next steps: SOP result review of LAB-0225 with a retest/invalidation decision, BATCH-075 disposition impact assessment, assay QC retrieval, and follow-up of the process-support-area alert. Proposed severity MEDIUM (advisory; the configured routing policy determines final severity). This investigation does not approve or execute any disposition, release, CAPA or manufacturing change.

workflow.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: four independent record systems carry BATCH-075 records on 2024-12-01 between 06:40Z and 11:10Z, and the lab-side systems express one normalized relative bioburden signal in three forms - absolute action-limit ratio (LIMS 1.23/0.79), a duplicated re-export (microbiology_results.xlsx), and percent-of-limit (lims_review_local 123.0%). The action-level peak (10:40Z sample) is bracketed by alert-level results (0.79 at 10:45Z, 0.71 environmental at 10:50Z) while historian margins stay within expected ranges; the only non-normal historian severity for this batch is 'low' on differential_pressure_margin (0.9615 vs high limit 1.0) at 09:10Z, a temporal association that establishes no causal direction. Systematic recording caveats: the package exports carry no elapsed process clocks (1049 of 1051 screened series flagged missing_source_time; the deterministic align_series check rejects LIMS-vs-historian alignment for lack of visible source time coordinates), so chronology rests on explicit zoned record timestamps. Two worksheets are re-exports of canonical LIMS data and provide no independent assurance; the scanned review document is an image-only PDF whose degraded OCR self-identifies as a duplicate export and remains pending human visual review. Cohort exceptions: LAB-0225 (1.23) exceeds every historical result; past action-level results either stood (LAB-0010, SYN-0004, 1.08) or were invalidated after review (LAB-0043, SYN-0014, 1.06), so both outcomes are precedented. Six further SYN entities carry historical alert-level results (all status alert, below the action limit), and each was followed by a substantially lower repeat result within about a day; for three of them the same-day environmental record is also elevated. All 15 related units were read at row level as cohort context. Missing evidence, not any confirmed cause, is the main limit: no assay QC, method/analyst metadata, reviewer identity/date, sampling SOP for the paired draws, retest results, or post-cutoff records are available in scope. All 311 screening units carry an explicit review disposition (34 investigated, 277 reviewed with no material signal).
